findings.description: [AI-SAST via Code Scan Verification Validation | claude-opus-5] The inconsistent-or-absent access control this CM addresses is not present; the module is a single centralised RBAC decision point. ROLE_PERMISSIONS states the whole model in one table with no inheritance and no wildcard, permissions_for() returns an empty set for any unrecognised role and has_permission() returns False for a null user or a user with no role, so every unanticipated case fails closed rather than raising a 500 that is mistaken for a refusal. Routes declare a Permission via the Requires dependency, which resolves the identity from the token through get_current_user, audits each denial with actor/role/action and returns a uniform opaque 403. Object-level authorization is covered by AuthzContext.require_ownership(), which decides against the resource loaded from the database rather than a client-supplied id, and by owned_by(), which narrows queries at the SQL level so a handler never holds another user's row. system_authz() is the only privileged escape hatch and is reachable solely from bootstrap seeding, never from request-influenced input | verdict=pass confidence=high
